issues.failure_explanation: For f,g with values in \T=\R/\Z, the expression t f(x) is not defined for nonintegral t\in[0,1]; scalar multiplication is not an operation on \R/\Z. The displayed computation also treats f_\gamma(1-0)-f_\gamma(0) as the integer degree, but f_\gamma is \T-valued, so f_\gamma(1-0)=f_\gamma(0); the degree belongs to the lift \bar f_\gamma. Thus the proposed homotopy is ill-defined and the converse direction is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the linear formula by a proof that a map with all listed winding numbers zero is null-homotopic, e.g. via [G,\T]\cong H^1(G;\Z) and the cell-boundary loops, then add that null-homotopy to g.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that equality of the full degree vector implies homotopy is not proved; later prose identifying homotopy classes with degree vectors rests on this unproved converse.
issues.title: thm.homotopy sufficiency uses an ill-defined linear homotopy on the circle
issues.why_classification: The statement is plausibly true and the necessity half works, but the sufficiency proof needs a contained nontrivial homotopy/null-homotopy argument rather than the displayed formula.

issues.failure_explanation: The conditions in \eqref{bc-hm} are differences of a lift and the degree vector is unchanged by f\mapsto f+c for a constant c\in\T; harmonicity is also translation-invariant. Hence any solution generates a circle of distinct solutions with identical stated data. The covering-space construction silently fixes this gauge by imposing f(v_1^k)=k, in particular f(v_1)=0 for k=0, but thm.main does not include that normalization.

failure_location.quote: There is a unique HM $f: G\to\T$ satisfying \eqref{bc-hm} and \eqref{homotopy-c}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the gauge already used in \eqref{def-H}, e.g. \bar f_{\gamma_0}(0)=0 equivalently f(v_1)=0, or else change the conclusion to uniqueness modulo additive constants.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness half of the main SG theorem is false as stated; abstract and discussion statements of a unique HM inherit the same overclaim.
issues.title: thm.main claims absolute uniqueness although the data are translation-invariant
issues.why_classification: A faithful repair must add a global normalization or weaken absolute uniqueness to uniqueness modulo constants; existence and the construction survive, but the stated guarantee is not a mere typo.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed claim quantifies over all \tilde V_m, but the discrete Laplacian is required to vanish only at interior nodes. At the copies v_i^k the values are prescribed by the boundary/jump data and need not satisfy the Laplace equation; the proof only checks the glued cut points.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the quantifier to interior nodes, e.g. \tilde V_m\setminus \tilde V_0, or explicitly say \tilde\Gamma_m-harmonic in the previously defined interior sense.
issues.overall_effect: As written, equation \eqref{G-harmonic} is false at boundary vertices; the intended interior-node harmonicity used later remains intact.
issues.title: lem.ext_harmonic_on_G states the discrete Laplace equation at boundary vertices too
issues.why_classification: This is a quantifier correction to the already-defined notion of graph harmonicity; no construction, rate, or downstream guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The real Dirichlet form uses squared differences, while \eqref{Em-hat} sums the unsquared geodesic distance. With the unsquared distance it is not the pulled-back Dirichlet form, the stated equality with E[\Gamma_m^0] is false, and at the (5/3)^m scaling the functional is generically divergent for nonconstant harmonic maps.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace d_\T(f(x),f(y)) by d_\T(f(x),f(y))^2; when |\mathbf f^\ast(\xi)-\mathbf f^\ast(\eta)|<\pi the squared geodesic distance equals the squared real difference, restoring the stated equality.
issues.overall_effect: The variational interpretation in Section\ref{sec.HM}, including the equality \hat\cE_m(\hat f_m^\ast)=E[\Gamma_m^0](\mathbf f^\ast) and the resulting unique-minimizer conclusion, is unsupported as written.
issues.title: the circle-valued energy Em-hat omits the square on the geodesic distance
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single missing square and it makes the functional consistent with the real Dirichlet form; the construction and guarantees survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The general assumptions require only that the cut point lie on the embedded i-th cycle and on no other embedded cycle. A point of V_{m+1} in a general p.c.f. fractal can be the intersection of several cells and can have more than two itineraries; then replacing it by two copies c_- and c_+ and making the stated identification is not guaranteed to be defined or to separate the two sides of the cycle. The proof imports the SG twofold cut construction outside its hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit simple-cut hypothesis: each \xi(\gamma_i^{(m)}) has exactly two itineraries, cutting it separates the two sides of \iota(\gamma_i^{(m)}), and the identification uses those two copies; verify this hypothesis in the examples, or else develop a branch-point cut-and-paste construction.
issues.overall_effect: The existence proof for general p.c.f. fractals has a gap precisely at the cut-and-identify step; the conditional theorem is not established for all p.c.f. fractals satisfying the stated basis assumptions.
issues.title: thm.pcf proof cuts at points that are not assumed to have two itineraries
issues.why_classification: A contained strengthening of the cut-point hypotheses may suffice and does not require new global proof architecture, but as stated the general p.c.f. construction is not well-defined for all permitted fractals.

issues.failure_explanation: For w\in S^m, the finite itinerary w13 has length m+2, so the displayed x_w,y_w,z_w lie in V_{m+2}, while the general construction puts the cut point for a cell w of length m in V_{m+1} and uses the shift \rho_{\ell(w)}. With the stated range 1\le m\le N, the appendix omits the level-one cuts, which would be x_\emptyset,y_\emptyset,z_\emptyset with shifts \rho_1,\rho_2,\rho_3, and includes an unneeded level N+1 family.

failure_location.quote: In addition, for every $1\le m\le N$ and $w\in S^m$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Range the parent word over |w|=0,\dots,N-1, equivalently replace $1\le m\le N$ by $0\le m\le N-1$; then x_\emptyset,y_\emptyset,z_\emptyset supply the level-one cuts and x_w,y_w,z_w supply the three child cuts of w.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit appendix formulae do not give the cut points required for the stated order-N construction; the general description in Section\ref{sec.higherorderSG} remains the controlling statement.
issues.title: appendix cut-point range is off by one relative to the higher-order construction
issues.why_classification: The defect is an off-by-one in the stated range; for the corrected range the displayed identifications match the general SG cut rule, so the repair is local and preserves the method.
